verdicts.justification: The exact repro (with -W always) produced NO PendingDeprecationWarning in this environment -- output was clean. Investigation: np.asmatrix IS still used (hypertools/align/procrustes.py:183, 'd = np.asmatrix(data)') and bare numpy 2.3.5 does warn on asmatrix, but importing hypertools installs a global warnings filter ('ignore', re.compile('the matrix subclass is not the recommended way', re.IGNORECASE), Warning) via its import chain, which suppresses the warning even under -W always. So no warning 'leaks on every call' as claimed; the np.matrix usage itself is real but silent here.
commands_run: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -W always -c "import hypertools as hyp; from hypertools.align.procrustes import procrustes; s = hyp.load('spiral'); r = procrustes(s[0], s[1]); print(type(r))"
.venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np; print(np.__version__); np.asmatrix(np.eye(3))"
.venv/bin/python -W always -c "import warnings; import hypertools; [print(f) for f in warnings.filters[:12]]"
grep -n 'matrix\|np\.mat' hypertools/align/procrustes.py

verdicts.justification: Reproduced: apply_model(60x8, 'KMeans') returned shape (60, 8) (cluster-distance space via transform) while hyp.cluster on the same data returned 60 labels. The behavior is documented (model.py:66-68: mode 'auto' "prefers predict_proba (fitting first), then fit_transform/transform, then fit_predict") -- KMeans has no predict_proba so transform wins.
